lines.text: Two days later, Kell brought us to his people.
The Skeld camp sat beneath a frozen cliff. Forty tents of white hide, around one small fire. Two hundred people. All of them cold.
An old man was feeding the fire with bones. In the White, even the wood is ice.
Seven died last moon. Four of them were children.
Then they saw the snow around my boots. Melting. Steaming. Running in little streams toward their fire.
And one by one, the Skeld went down on their knees.
No. Please, get up. I'm not anybody. I'm a zero.
Nobody got up. I don't think I have ever hated anything so much.
They don't kneel to you, boy. They kneel to the warmth. You just happen to be standing in it.
She was small and very old, and her eyes were as white as the snow. Kell said Yrsa had been blind since birth, and saw more than anyone in the White.
Behind me, the children crept up and held their hands over my footprints, as if they were a hearth.
Come here, Warm One. Let me look at you.
She put her hands on my face. They were like ice. And then they weren't.
Hm. Everyone has a cup inside them, big or small. You have no cup at all. Only the water, pouring out.
The Sleeping Queen poured like that, once. Before she slept.
Kell had told us about her on the road. The Skeld believed a queen slept beneath the White, and the cold was her dreaming.
Behind Yrsa, one Skeld had not knelt. A big woman in a bear's skin, with the bear's head for a hood.
I am Freydis, first of the elders. Kneeling is for the desperate, southerner. The White does not run on miracles. It runs on law.
In the crowd, a small boy with red-brown hair was staring at Wren. Wren was staring back. I didn't think anything of it. Not then.
Skeld law. A guest who would sit at our fire must first feed it. Tomorrow, Warm One, you hunt.
I had never hunted anything in my life. Unless you count books.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter thirty-three, coming soon.
